Genomic sampling maps · Public genomic inventory · Genomic summary for these species

80 species with at least 50 dated specimens through 1930 in the western Atlantic, Caribbean and Gulf of Mexico. Eligibility sums specimens across stages. Undated specimens do not confer eligibility.

Every map uses the same extent: 100°W to 50°W longitude, 5°N to 60°N latitude. Grid: 2° × 2°. No zooming or cropping between species, stages or years.

One map per species combines all eligible years and all life stages, including undated lots. Numbered cells connect to their collection-year labels; parentheses show specimen counts for that cell and year. Colors show total specimens per cell, not abundance. Enlarge labels for a scrollable view; the geographic extent stays fixed.

Hatched cells include approximate locations. Missing coordinates are estimated from station, locality, island or broader location labels. These display positions can be much less precise than a grid cell; they are not verified collecting sites. Frame counts separate recorded coordinates from estimates. Original coordinates remain unchanged, and estimates are excluded from precise-location candidate screens.

Adults / non-larval, larvae and mixed lots are pooled on these maps. Undated samples are included and labeled Undated in their cells. Use the year-by-year atlas to inspect stages separately.

Species traits: curated life-history, trophic and functional summaries, including FishBase release 26.06, supplementary literature and source-specific reef classifications where available. Model-derived ages are labeled separately from reported ages. Independent scientific review remains pending. Source citations and evidence are expandable within each species card. Species illustrations: 54 locally saved images with credits and noncommercial reuse terms; other entries link to their sources with review notes. Illustrations are representative of the species, not the sampled museum lots. Image sources and credits

Order and family follow the museum catalog labels, which may differ from current classifications. Common names come from cached FishBase records using the existing curated species matches, including approved synonyms or proxies; unresolved matches remain unreported. Genomic data filters

Contemporary means a reported collection year after 1930. Worldwide counts include records needing biological review. Regional candidates pass the date, coordinate and biological screens in the Atlantic–Caribbean–Gulf window. These species-level filters are independent of the historical stage and region filters.

Species trait filters

Combine traits with the sampling filters above. Different fields must all match. Water types and habitat tags test membership in positive records; an unlisted tag is not evidence of absence. Missing or withheld values remain visible until an active trait filter excludes them.

A minimum exceeds its maximum. Correct the range to show matching species.

Model ages and reported ages are separate fields. Trophic level prefers the diet estimate, then food items; methods are not averaged. Source-specific feeding classes and reef guilds remain separate. Missing traits do not mean biological absence. IUCN categories are dated source snapshots, not verified latest status. Lengths take the largest reported value across sexes separately for each type; TL, SL and FL are not converted. Numeric bounds apply to the named summary field, not to all population-level observations.

Filters refine the 80 eligible species using dated records through 1930. Specimen counts and distinct years must meet the thresholds within the selected stage and region together. Undated specimens do not count toward these filters.

Filters select species; maps always show all their included years, regions and life stages. The stage, region and coordinate controls only affect the candidate thresholds. Undated lots appear on maps but do not count toward those thresholds.

No species match these filters. Lower the thresholds or reset the filters.
